summary: Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) was an Indologist and historian who served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested in 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Druzhinin is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2003–2009) and Peoples' Friendship University of Russia (2013–2016), later working as an assistant at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2009) and Novosibirsk State University (2015).

Vladimir Ivanov Georgiev (1908–1986) was a linguist who studied under Stefan Mladenov at Sofia University and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. He spent his career at Sofia University, serving as Head of Linguistics from 1945 to 1974.

Vladimir Ivanovich Kalyanov (1908–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Leningrad Institute of History, Philosophy and Linguistics under Aleksej Barannikov and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from 1937 to 1985.

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages. His major posts included Professor of Persian Studies at SOAS (1937–1944) and teaching at Cairo University.

Vladimir Nikolaevich Toporov (1928–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson and later worked at the Institute of Slavic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences as a researcher starting in 1954.

Vladimir P. Ivanov is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a senior researcher at the St. Petersburg Institute for Informatics and Automation (1989) and as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies (attested 2009).

Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij (1927–1956) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vladimir Tikhonov (born 1973) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, Moscow State University, and Korea University, and he has served as a professor at the University of Oslo since 2006.

Vladimír Miltner (1933–1997) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his Ph.D. studies at Charles University between 1952 and 1967 and worked as a research scholar at the Czech Academy of Sciences in 1967.

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who studied under David P. Jackson at the University of Hamburg and Franz-Karl Ehrhard at the University of Munich. His career includes posts at the University of Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and University of Bern.

Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) is a historian who studied at Kiel University and Chiang Mai University. He served as Professor of Southeast Asian History at the University of Münster (1999) before becoming Chair of Thai Studies at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz (born 1956) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and under Anagarika Govinda. He held academic positions at the University of Vienna, Otani University, Ryukoku University, and the University of Luxembourg.

Vrajavallabha Dvivedi (1926–2012) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He headed the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and served as Deputy Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–1992).
Vriti Sharma is a researcher in computational fields and Indology. She has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Vsevolod Bronislavovich Tomashevsky (1891–1927) was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Jan Baudouin de Courtenay and Vincenz Scherzl. He taught at Baku State University before becoming Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Rector at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vsevolod Miller (1848–1913) was a scholar of Iranian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Moscow State University under Pavel Petrov and Fyodor Buslaev, later becoming Docent at Moscow University, Director of the Lazarev Institute, and an Academician.

Vsevolod Sergeevič Semencov (1941–1986) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Moscow State University and Banaras Hindu University, later working as a researcher at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1968–1984) and the Institute of Philosophy (1984).

Vyacheslav Ivanov (1929–2017) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhaïl Peterson and Pyotr Kuznetsov. He held posts at the Institute of Slavic Studies, Russian State University for the Humanities, and UCLA.

Vydūnas (1868–1953) was a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at universities including Königsberg, Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Berlin, where he also taught Lithuanian from 1917 to 1919 and held a post at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen.
